claim: The European Research Council (ERC) focuses solely on scientific excellence when assessing grant proposals.
source: The sole focus at the ERC is on scientific excellence.
evidence: Direct statement from ERC spokesperson quoted in the manuscript.

claim: The ERC aims to recognize the best ideas and confer status and visibility on the best brains in Europe while attracting talent from abroad.
source: The aim is to recognize the best ideas, and confer status and visibility on the best brains in Europe, while also attracting talent from abroad," says a spokesperson for the council.
evidence: Direct quote from ERC spokesperson describing the council's aims.

claim: Two-thirds of ERC grants went to researchers based in just five countries (UK, Germany, France, the Netherlands and Switzerland) between 2007 and 2013.
source: Some critics have claimed that this strategy unfairly favors researchers based at institutions in wealthier nations, with two-thirds of ERC grants going to researchers based in just five countries – the UK, Germany, France, the Netherlands and Switzerland – between 2007 and 2013.
evidence: Statistical data about ERC grant distribution cited from critics' claims.

claim: Critics claim that the ERC's strategy unfairly favors researchers based at institutions in wealthier nations.
source: Some critics have claimed that this strategy unfairly favors researchers based at institutions in wealthier nations, with two-thirds of ERC grants going to researchers based in just five countries – the UK, Germany, France, the Netherlands and Switzerland – between 2007 and 2013.
evidence: Statement attributed to critics regarding perceived bias in ERC funding.

claim: The ERC's peer review evaluation process has been designed to identify scientific excellence irrespective of gender, age, nationality, institution of the principal investigator, and other potential biases.
source: The peer review evaluation process has been carefully designed to identify scientific excellence irrespective of the gender, age, nationality or institution of the principal investigator and other potential biases.
evidence: Direct statement from ERC spokesperson about the design of their peer review process.

claim: The ERC takes career breaks and unconventional career paths into account when awarding grants.
source: The ERC also takes career breaks and "unconventional career paths" into account when awarding grants.
evidence: Statement about ERC policy regarding career considerations.

claim: Most funding agencies other than the ERC use two or more criteria to assess research proposals.
source: Most other funding agencies use two or more criteria to assess research proposals.
evidence: Comparative statement about funding agency practices based on the manuscript's survey of multiple agencies.

claim: The National Science Foundation (NSF) is the primary source of federal funding for non-medical basic research in the US.
source: The National Science Foundation (NSF) – the primary source of federal funding for non-medical basic research in the US – assesses all applications on two major criteria: intellectual merit and broader impacts.
evidence: Descriptive statement about NSF's role in US research funding.

claim: The NSF assesses all applications on two major criteria: intellectual merit and broader impacts.
source: The National Science Foundation (NSF) – the primary source of federal funding for non-medical basic research in the US – assesses all applications on two major criteria: intellectual merit and broader impacts.
evidence: Direct statement about NSF assessment criteria.

claim: The broader impacts criterion at NSF encompasses the potential to benefit society and contribute to the achievement of specific, desired societal outcomes.
source: The broader impacts criterion encompasses the potential to benefit society and contribute to the achievement of specific, desired societal outcomes," says Rob Margetta, a public affairs specialist at the NSF.
evidence: Direct quote from NSF official defining the broader impacts criterion.

claim: Cancer Research UK is the world's largest cancer research charity.
source: Cancer Research UK – the world's largest cancer research charity – assesses the expertise of the research team submitting the proposal and the originality of the ideas along with several other criteria including the relevance to the charity's current research priorities, the quality of the experimental design, and value for money.
evidence: Descriptive statement about Cancer Research UK's status.

claim: Cancer Research UK assesses the expertise of the research team, originality of ideas, relevance to current research priorities, quality of experimental design, and value for money.
source: Cancer Research UK – the world's largest cancer research charity – assesses the expertise of the research team submitting the proposal and the originality of the ideas along with several other criteria including the relevance to the charity's current research priorities, the quality of the experimental design, and value for money.
evidence: Direct statement about Cancer Research UK's assessment criteria.

claim: Cancer Research UK outlines its assessment criteria on its website so that applicants understand what they will be judged on.
source: The criteria are outlined on our website," says Matt Kaiser, head of discovery research at the charity, "so that applicants really understand what they will be judged on.
evidence: Direct quote from Cancer Research UK official about transparency of criteria.

claim: Different funding schemes at the Australian Research Council (ARC) employ different criteria to assess applications.
source: At the Australian Research Council (ARC), different funding schemes employ different criteria to assess applications.
evidence: Direct statement about ARC's variable assessment approach.

claim: In ARC's early career researcher scheme, the investigator and project quality and innovation are the two major criteria, accounting for 75% of the assessment score.
source: For example, in a scheme that supports early career researchers, the investigator themselves and "project quality and innovation" are the two major criteria, accounting for 75% of the assessment score.
evidence: Specific data about weighting of criteria in ARC's early career scheme.

claim: In ARC schemes that promote collaborations with industry and other partners, emphasis is placed on commitment from partner organizations and project significance and innovation, with investigator criteria carrying less weight.
source: However, in schemes that promote collaborations with industry and other partners, emphasis is placed on the commitment from partner organizations and project significance and innovation, with the investigators criteria carrying less weight.
evidence: Statement about criteria weighting in ARC's collaborative schemes.

claim: The ARC takes into account researchers who are early in their career or have had interrupted research careers due to employment outside academia, unemployment, child birth, carers' responsibilities and other personal circumstances.
source: Researchers who are early in their research career or have had an interrupted research career – including employment outside academia, unemployment, child birth, carers' responsibilities and other personal circumstances – will have this taken into account," says Leanne Harvey, who is the council's executive general manager.
evidence: Direct quote from ARC official about consideration of career circumstances.

claim: All proposals for ARC funding pass through the same peer review process despite using different sets of criteria for different funding schemes.
source: Despite using different sets of criteria for different funding schemes, all proposals for ARC funding pass through the same peer review process.
evidence: Direct statement about uniformity of ARC's peer review process.

claim: In the ARC peer review process, two or more Detailed Assessors provide written assessments and ratings based on relevant criteria.
source: Firstly, two or more Detailed Assessors – researchers who have expertise in the same field as the proposal – provide written assessments and ratings based on the relevant criteria.
evidence: Description of the first step in ARC's peer review process.

claim: ARC applicants are given the opportunity to provide feedback on Detailed Assessors' assessments before the application is passed to General Assessors.
source: The applicants are then given the opportunity to provide feedback on these assessments before the application is passed on to two or more General Assessors, who are researchers working in the same or related fields.
evidence: Description of applicant feedback opportunity in ARC process.

claim: ARC General Assessors use their expertise and broader knowledge of research planning to examine written assessments and applicant feedback and give each application an initial assessment score.
source: The General Assessors use their own expertise, plus their broader knowledge of research planning and other issues, to examine the written assessments and applicant feedback and give each application an initial assessment score.
evidence: Description of General Assessors' role in ARC process.

claim: Initial scores from ARC General Assessors are used to produce a ranked list of proposals for a committee to discuss.
source: The initial scores are used to produce a ranked list of proposals for a committee of General Assessors to discuss.
evidence: Description of how initial scores are used in ARC process.

claim: The ARC committee makes recommendations that are considered by the CEO and then passed to the Minister, who determines which proposals should be funded.
source: This committee makes recommendations that are considered by the CEO and then passed on to the Minister, who determines which proposals should be funded.
evidence: Description of final decision-making process at ARC.

claim: The NSF received 49,620 research proposals in the 2015 fiscal year.
source: Virtually all applications submitted to the NSF, which received a staggering 49,620 research proposals in the 2015 fiscal year alone, are independently evaluated by at least three external experts who provide written assessments.
evidence: Specific numerical data about NSF proposal volume.

claim: Virtually all NSF applications are independently evaluated by at least three external experts who provide written assessments.
source: Virtually all applications submitted to the NSF, which received a staggering 49,620 research proposals in the 2015 fiscal year alone, are independently evaluated by at least three external experts who provide written assessments.
evidence: Statement about NSF's peer review process.

claim: An NSF program officer examines external expert assessments and makes recommendations for funding.
source: An NSF program officer examines these assessments and makes recommendations for funding.
evidence: Description of program officer role in NSF process.

claim: Before an NSF application can be funded, it must be signed off by the relevant division director and reviewed for business, financial and policy implications by another NSF official.
source: Before an application can be funded it must be signed off by the relevant division director and then reviewed for business, financial and policy implications by another NSF official.
evidence: Description of NSF's approval requirements before funding.

claim: Cancer Research UK and the ERC often use two-step peer review processes to reduce the burden on external reviewers.
source: Other funding agencies, including Cancer Research UK (CRUK) and the ERC, often use two-step peer review processes to reduce the burden on external reviewers.
evidence: Statement about the rationale for two-step processes at these agencies.

claim: In two-step peer review processes, a panel of external experts initially screens proposals based on an outline or summary.
source: A panel of external experts who work in the relevant research fields initially screens the proposals based on an outline or summary.
evidence: Description of first step in two-step peer review process.

claim: In two-step peer review processes, only proposals that pass the first stage are sent to two or more independent experts for detailed reviews on full applications.
source: Only the proposals that pass this first stage are sent to two or more independent experts, who are asked to provide detailed reviews on the full applications.
evidence: Description of second step in two-step peer review process.

claim: In two-step peer review processes, the original panel examines detailed reviews and makes the final decision about whether to fund the research.
source: The original panel then examines these reviews and is responsible for making the final decision about whether to fund the research.
evidence: Description of final decision-making in two-step peer review process.

claim: For large grant applications to Cancer Research UK, the panel may interview the applicant, providing opportunity to discuss and counter any concerns.
source: For large grant applications to CRUK, the panel may also interview the applicant, providing him or her with the opportunity to discuss and counter any concerns.
evidence: Description of interview option in CRUK's process for large grants.

claim: Cancer Research UK seeks between three and six written reviews for most grants, depending on the size of the award.
source: For most grants, and depending on the size of the award, we seek anywhere between three and six written reviews," says Kaiser of CRUK.
evidence: Direct quote from CRUK official about number of reviewers.

claim: Two people assessing the same research proposal can come to different conclusions, making it difficult for decision makers to score the proposal and rank it against others.
source: The number of reviewers is an important consideration because two people assessing the same research proposal can come to different conclusions, making it difficult for decision makers to score the proposal and rank it against others.
evidence: Statement about variability in peer review assessments.

claim: A 2012 study examining data on peer review at the Fonds zur Förderung der wissenschaftlichen Forschung in Austria recommended that bioscience research proposals should be assessed by a minimum of three independent reviewers to help compensate for variation in assessments.
source: In 2012, a study that examined data on peer review at the Fonds zur Förderung der wissenschaftlichen Forschung in Austria recommended that bioscience research proposals should be assessed by a minimum of three independent reviewers to help compensate for this variation (Mutz et al., 2012).
evidence: Citation of a specific study with its findings and recommendations.

claim: Funding agencies need to ensure that reviewers follow the agency's policies and apply its selection criteria correctly.
source: Once a funding agency has recruited reviewers, it needs to ensure that they follow the agency's policies and apply its selection criteria correctly.
evidence: General statement about funding agency responsibilities.

claim: At the ERC, the President briefs the chairs of its 25 peer review panels on key principles of the evaluation process, including policy on gender balance, measures on widening participation, conflicts of interest and matters of confidentiality.
source: At the ERC this starts with the President of the council briefing the chairs of its 25 peer review panels on the key principles of the ERC evaluation process, including its policy on gender balance, measures on widening participation, conflicts of interest and matters of confidentiality.
evidence: Description of ERC's process for ensuring proper reviewer conduct.

claim: Cancer Research UK is a member of the Association of Medical Research Charities.
source: As a member of the Association of Medical Research Charities, CRUK is bound by the association's principles of peer review.
evidence: Statement about CRUK's organizational membership.

claim: Cancer Research UK is bound by the Association of Medical Research Charities' principles of peer review.
source: As a member of the Association of Medical Research Charities, CRUK is bound by the association's principles of peer review.
evidence: Statement about CRUK's obligations as a member organization.

claim: Cancer Research UK's review processes are independent, impartial, balanced, accountable and include a diversity of opinion.
source: This means our review processes are independent, impartial, balanced, accountable and include a diversity of opinion," says Kaiser.
evidence: Direct quote from CRUK official describing their review process characteristics.

claim: Cancer Research UK's review processes are audited every five years to ensure they meet the Association of Medical Research Charities' requirements.
source: To ensure CRUK is meeting these requirements, the charity's review processes are audited every five years.
evidence: Statement about CRUK's quality assurance process.

claim: The Volkswagen Foundation is a private research agency founded in 1962 in Germany.
source: The Volkswagen Foundation – a private research agency founded in 1962 in Germany – has been testing out alternative ways to assess applications for some of its funding schemes.
evidence: Factual statement about the foundation's establishment.

claim: The Volkswagen Foundation has been testing alternative ways to assess applications for some of its funding schemes.
source: The Volkswagen Foundation – a private research agency founded in 1962 in Germany – has been testing out alternative ways to assess applications for some of its funding schemes.
evidence: Statement about the foundation's experimental approaches.

claim: The Experiment! scheme supports researchers in science and engineering who want to investigate daring new ideas.
source: For example, in the Experiment! scheme, which supports researchers in science and engineering who want to investigate daring new ideas, double-blind peer review ensures that the interdisciplinary jury reviewing the applications assesses the quality of the idea and not the reputation of the person behind it.
evidence: Description of the Experiment! scheme's purpose.

claim: The Experiment! scheme uses double-blind peer review to ensure the interdisciplinary jury assesses the quality of the idea and not the reputation of the person behind it.
source: For example, in the Experiment! scheme, which supports researchers in science and engineering who want to investigate daring new ideas, double-blind peer review ensures that the interdisciplinary jury reviewing the applications assesses the quality of the idea and not the reputation of the person behind it.
evidence: Statement about the rationale for double-blind review in Experiment! scheme.

claim: Funding decisions for Experiment! grants could be biased towards fields that the jury are more familiar with because the grants are so broad in scope.
source: Since Experiment! grants are so broad in scope it is possible that funding decisions could be biased towards fields that the jury are more familiar with.
evidence: Statement acknowledging potential bias in the Experiment! scheme.

claim: The Volkswagen Foundation is currently running a trial that uses a lottery to increase the diversity of proposals they fund in the Experiment! scheme.
source: To address this issue, the Volkswagen Foundation is currently running a trial that uses a lottery to increase the diversity of the proposals they fund.
evidence: Statement about the foundation's experimental lottery approach.

claim: In the Volkswagen Foundation's lottery trial, the foundation first screens applications to ensure they address the program criteria.
source: First, the foundation screens the applications to make sure that they address the program criteria.
evidence: Description of first step in the lottery trial process.

claim: In the Volkswagen Foundation's lottery trial, anonymized versions of shortlisted applications are passed to the jury, which rejects any that are not of sufficient quality.
source: Anonymized versions of the shortlisted applications are then passed to the jury, which rejects any that are not of sufficient quality.
evidence: Description of jury review step in the lottery trial process.

claim: In the Volkswagen Foundation's lottery trial, the jury selects the most convincing ideas from the pool of good quality proposals to receive funding.
source: From the pool of good quality proposals that remains, the jury selects the ideas they find most convincing to receive funding.
evidence: Description of jury selection step in the lottery trial process.

claim: In the Volkswagen Foundation's lottery trial, good quality proposals not selected by the jury have a second chance to be awarded funding through a lottery overseen by the foundation's legal officer.
source: The other good quality proposals have a second chance to be awarded funding through the lottery overseen by the foundation's legal officer.
evidence: Description of lottery mechanism in the trial process.

claim: The Volkswagen Foundation hopes the lottery approach will uncover projects which otherwise are easily overlooked.
source: In this way the foundation hopes to "uncover projects which otherwise are easily overlooked," says program director Ulrike Bischler.
evidence: Direct quote from foundation official about the goal of the lottery approach.

claim: The partial randomization approach might be used in more Volkswagen Foundation funding initiatives in the future, depending on the results of an independent evaluation.
source: Depending on the results of an independent evaluation, this partial randomization approach might be used in more funding initiatives in the future.
evidence: Statement about potential future use of the lottery approach contingent on evaluation results.

claim: Once a researcher receives a grant, they will need to do the research they promised to do.
source: Once a researcher has received his or her grant they will need to do the research that they promised to do.
evidence: Statement about post-funding expectations.

claim: If research goes well, researchers will submit results to a journal where they will be scrutinized by two or more peers.
source: If all goes well, they will submit the results to a journal – where, once again, they will find themselves under scrutiny from two or more of their peers.
evidence: Statement about the publication process following funded research.

claim: Funding agencies use many different criteria and peer review strategies to assess grant proposals.
source: Funding agencies use many different criteria and peer review strategies to assess grant proposals.
evidence: Abstract statement summarizing the main topic of the manuscript.
